boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of California-San Diego, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A self-guided first-weekend art walk across ten permanent Stuart Collection works, moving from Geisel Library through central campus and toward the arts district.

cards.title: Start among the lead-skinned trees
cards.subtitle: Terry Allen’s 1986 work near Geisel Library
cards.notes: Begin at the eucalyptus grove between Geisel Library and the Faculty Club. Pause to spot the lead-covered trees and listen for their intermittent sound works.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor sound-and-sculpture encounter that rewards a slow first pass.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego identifies Trees (1986) in the eucalyptus grove between Geisel Library and the Faculty Club; two preserved trees emit recorded music, poems, and stories.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork; the source notes that the sound works include periods of silence.

cards.title: Meet at Geisel’s main entrance
cards.subtitle: John Baldessari’s 2001 installation
cards.notes: Continue to Geisel Library’s main entrance and look up at the colorful installation. Use it as a clear rendezvous point before continuing across campus.
cards.short_summary: A named artwork integrated with Geisel’s main entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego lists John Baldessari’s READ/WRITE/THINK/DREAM (2001) at the Geisel Library main entrance.
cards.access_notes: Located at the library’s main entrance; follow campus access guidance for the building.

cards.title: Cross to Revelle Plaza
cards.subtitle: Mark Bradford’s 2018 light sculpture
cards.notes: Walk south to Revelle Plaza and view the slender galvanized-steel column from a few distances. Its luminaire changes with surrounding light conditions.
cards.short_summary: A tall, site-specific work marking Revelle Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego locates Mark Bradford’s What Hath God Wrought (2018) in Revelle Plaza and describes its galvanized-steel pole and adjustable luminaire.
cards.source_title: Mark Bradford — What Hath God Wrought

cards.title: Follow the KAHNOP pathway
cards.subtitle: Ann Hamilton’s 2023 work by the amphitheater
cards.notes: Head toward the Epstein Family Amphitheater and walk the basalt pathway at a reading pace. Look down for raised and engraved language in the route.
cards.short_summary: A long text-bearing pathway beside the campus trolley area.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego locates Ann Hamilton’s KAHNOP • TO TELL A STORY (2023) near Epstein Family Amphitheater, between Russell Lane and Central Trolley Station.
cards.source_title: Ann Hamilton — KAHNOP • TO TELL A STORY
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pathway near the amphitheater and Central Trolley Station.

cards.title: Find the stone Bear
cards.subtitle: Tim Hawkinson’s 2005 work at Jacobs Engineering
cards.notes: Make a short detour through the Jacobs School of Engineering academic courtyard. Circle the large stone bear to take in its scale and texture.
cards.short_summary: A documented stone bear in an engineering courtyard.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego lists Tim Hawkinson’s Bear (2005) in the Academic Courtyard at the Jacobs School of Engineering.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork in the Jacobs School of Engineering academic courtyard.

cards.title: Read the Green Table together
cards.subtitle: Jenny Holzer’s 1992 Muir College work
cards.notes: Continue to Muir College Quad and approach the granite table and benches. Read the inscribed text in small groups, leaving room for other users.
cards.short_summary: A granite table-and-benches artwork inscribed with text.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego identifies Jenny Holzer’s Green Table (1992) at Muir College Quad and describes it as a large granite table and benches inscribed with texts.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork in Muir College Quad.

cards.title: Step inside Price Center for Another
cards.subtitle: Barbara Kruger’s 2008 site-specific work
cards.notes: Use Price Center East as an indoor pause. Find the work on the west interior wall and take a moment to read its direct public-address text.
cards.short_summary: An indoor Stuart Collection work at Price Center East.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego locates Barbara Kruger’s Another (2008) on the west interior wall of Price Center East.
cards.access_notes: Interior artwork; building access may vary with campus operations.

cards.title: Look for the neon at Warren College
cards.subtitle: Bruce Nauman’s 1988 work
cards.notes: Continue to the Powell Structure Systems Laboratory in Warren College. View the installation from outside and give its shifting words time to register.
cards.short_summary: A site-specific neon work at Warren College.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego lists Bruce Nauman’s Vices and Virtues (1988) at the Powell Structure Systems Laboratory in Warren College.
cards.access_notes: Located at the Powell Structure Systems Laboratory; view from public exterior areas.

cards.title: Walk to Standing at the School of Medicine
cards.subtitle: Kiki Smith’s 1998 work near Biomedical Sciences
cards.notes: Take the route to the School of Medicine and find the work near the Biomedical Sciences Building. Notice how it sits among paths, lawns, and eucalyptus.
cards.short_summary: A permanent artwork positioned along School of Medicine foot traffic.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego locates Kiki Smith’s Standing (1998) at the School of Medicine near the Biomedical Sciences Building.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork near School of Medicine buildings.

cards.title: Finish behind La Jolla Playhouse
cards.subtitle: William Wegman’s 1988 panoramic work
cards.notes: End near La Jolla Playhouse and locate the installation behind it. Take in the setting, then use the official artwork page’s photo record to compare details.
cards.short_summary: A named Stuart Collection stop in the campus arts district.
cards.evidence_claim: UC San Diego identifies William Wegman’s La Jolla Vista View (1988) as located behind La Jolla Playhouse.
cards.source_title: William Wegman — La Jolla Vista View
cards.access_notes: Outdoor work behind La Jolla Playhouse.
